correction.statement: The strongest bounded-occurrence normalization relevant here is not exactly-3-literal SAT with at most three occurrences: that class is always satisfiable. Tovey's NP-complete frontier uses clauses of size 2 or 3 with at most three occurrences per variable.
correction.source: Craig A. Tovey, A simplified NP-complete satisfiability problem, Discrete Applied Mathematics 8 (1984), Theorem 2.1 and Theorem 2.4.
correction.consequence: The universal GF(2) decision frontier can be tightened from direction-rank <=4 to direction-rank <=3, provided both 2-clause and 3-clause determinant blocks are admitted.

construction.false_indicator: positive literal x_i -> 1+x_i; negative literal NOT x_i -> x_i
construction.global_pencil: M_F(x)=blockdiag of all G2/G3 clause blocks = M0 + sum_i x_i A_i
construction.decision_identity: For every Boolean assignment a, det M_F(a)=1 iff every clause is satisfied. Hence F is satisfiable iff the affine GF(2) pencil has a nonsingular Boolean completion.
construction.rank_bound: Each occurrence of x_i contributes one elementary entry in a distinct clause block. Therefore rank(A_i)=occ(x_i)<=3 in Tovey's bounded-occurrence normal form.

irreducible_switch_form.pure_variables: Any variable whose occurrences all have the same sign can be assigned to satisfy every incident clause and removed.
irreducible_switch_form.degree_one_two: Standard unit/pure/resolution preprocessing removes trivial low-degree structure; the hard boundary occurs when a degree-3 variable has both signs.
irreducible_switch_form.degree_three_mixed: Up to negating the variable, every irreducible degree-3 variable has polarity pattern (2 positive,1 negative). Its two Boolean states therefore choose between satisfying a 2-occurrence side and satisfying a 1-occurrence side.
irreducible_switch_form.name: RANK3_2_VS_1_BOOLEAN_SWITCH

algorithmic_boundary.rank1: Rank-one generated symbolic matrix rank admits polynomial machinery (matroid-intersection/Wong-sequence regime).
algorithmic_boundary.rank2: Rank-two skew-symmetric structure corresponds to linear matroid parity and remains polynomially tractable.
algorithmic_boundary.rank3: The present clause-block construction is already NP-hard at three occurrences. Thus a generic rank-3-to-rank-2 conversion cannot be assumed; any successful conversion must exploit the exact clause-block/signed-switch structure and preserve Boolean completion exactly.
algorithmic_boundary.current_live_question: Can every RANK3_2_VS_1_BOOLEAN_SWITCH be eliminated or lifted to a polynomially solvable rank-2/Pfaffian/matroid object with polynomial total size, exact SAT equivalence, and witness reconstruction?

next_target.name: E8_RANK3_SWITCH_TO_TRACTABLE_LIFT_V1_5
next_target.directive: Attack only the mixed degree-3 2-vs-1 switch. Seek a polynomial-size exact lift into a tractable linear-matroid-parity/Pfaffian/Wong-sequence class. Reject any lift that introduces exponentially many states, duplicates one switch into an unbounded number of independent choices, or loses Boolean tying of the three occurrences.
success_obligations: arbitrary 2/3-CNF with at most three occurrences after polynomial normalization
no hidden exponential branching, dimension, coefficient size, or oracle

scientific_ceiling.NEW_EXACT_FRONTIER: GF(2) clause-block affine nonsingularity with rank(A_i)<=3 and 2/3-clause blocks; irreducible atom is a 2-vs-1 degree-3 switch.
